title: Bridging Neural Representations and Symbolic Semantics in Audio Classification
abstract: arXiv:2610.40414v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Deep audio classifiers can achieve strong predictive performance, but their hidden representations remain difficult to interpret. Existing audio explainability methods often focus on input-level attribution, such as waveform segments, spectrogram regions, or acoustic features, and provide limited insight into what hidden neurons encode. Interpreting hidden neurons at the concept level can provide a more meaningful view of what an audio model learns internally. This paper investigates whether hidden neurons in audio classifiers can be associated with human-understandable symbolic acoustic concepts. A model-agnostic neurosymbolic framework is presented for analyzing the final hidden layer of audio classifiers, containing 32 neurons, through symbolic concept induction. The framework is evaluated on two audio classification settings: music genre classification using GTZAN dataset and musical instrument classification using IRMAS dataset. R

translated_title: 在音频分类中桥接神经表示与符号语义
translated_abstract: 深度音频分类器可以实现强大的预测性能，但其隐藏表示仍然难以解释。现有的音频可解释性方法通常关注输入级别的归因，例如波形片段、频谱图区域或声学特征，而对隐藏神经元编码的内容所提供的洞察有限。在概念层面解释隐藏神经元可以更有意义地展现音频模型内部学习到了什么。本文研究了音频分类器中的隐藏神经元是否可以与人类可理解的符号化声学概念相关联。文章提出了一个模型无关的神经符号框架，通过符号概念归纳来分析音频分类器的最终隐藏层（包含32个神经元）。该框架在两种音频分类设置上进行了评估：使用GTZAN数据集的音乐流派分类和使用IRMAS数据集的乐器分类。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个模型无关的神经符号框架，通过符号概念归纳将音频分类器隐藏层神经元与人类可理解的声学概念相关联，并在音乐流派分类和乐器分类任务上验证了该方法的有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a model-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that associates hidden neurons in audio classifiers with human-understandable symbolic acoustic concepts through concept induction, validated on music genre classification (GTZAN) and instrument classification (IRMAS) tasks.
